methods.description: Authenticate 66 issue contract pins and 62 nested historical Git pins; compare actual consumed scope, issue snapshot, builder, geometry and DZS bytes at read boundaries; run pinned builder from frozen verified bytes in private scratch; publish exclusively after successful computation. Five controls inject coherent two-file scope/snapshot drift and individual scope, snapshot, builder and source drift, plus preservation controls.
methods.software: Python 3.12 standard library and Git; runner self-binds to its committed blob; predecessor builder and helper execute from exact pinned Git blobs.
methods.units: whole-file bytes, SHA-256, unique Atlas location IDs, and byte equality of report outputs; no geometry measurements

summaries.text: The preserved workload contains exactly 224 unique Atlas location IDs.

conclusions.text: The captured #1209 request defines this reproduction scope as 224 exact subjects.
Two runs reproduced all three reports byte-identically to each other and both retained #1199 outputs; this establishes input-byte and report reproducibility only.

Official parentage, legal census-date boundaries, coastline/island completeness, seven unmatched roster units, four label candidates, geometry-type differences, and geoBoundaries file-specific reuse remain unresolved.
